title: Distinguished section of the closed-point vanishing-ideal quotient
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $U$ be an open subset, and let $x\in U$ have closed singleton. Put $Z=X\setminus U$ and $Z^{\prime}=Z\cup\{x\}$. Let $I$ and $J$ be the reduced vanishing ideal sheaves of $Z$ and $Z^{\prime}$ [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme], represented as $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $i:J\to I$ be their canonical inclusion and $Q=\operatorname{coker}(i)$. There exists $q\in\Gamma(X,Q)$ such that every $s\in\Gamma(X,I)$ whose image in $Q$ is $q$ has residue $1$ at $x$ after inclusion in $\mathcal O_X$ [def-weil-residue-field]. No existence of a global lift of $q$ is assumed or asserted, and U need not be affine.

source.place: Tag 01XF, label lemma-quasi-compact-h1-zero-covering, first paragraph before the H1 lifting step; read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01XF

proof.text: Let Z be X minus U and Z prime be Z union the closed singleton x. Take the concrete reduced vanishing ideals I and J. Their sectionwise descriptions by zero residue evaluations show that 1 on U is in I(U), so lift it through the injective inclusion of I into the structure sheaf to a section sU.

Take the existing canonical inclusion i = IdealSheafData.toModulesOfLE and its categorical cokernel Q. On V = X minus {x}, the reduced vanishing ideal descriptions give equality of I and J on every open contained in V. Prove the restriction of i is an isomorphism by injectivity and surjectivity on all sections. Restriction preserves cokernels, so Q restricted to V is zero. Evaluation and restrictAppIso give subsingleton sections of Q on every W contained in V.

The quotient image qU of sU on U and the zero section on V agree on both overlaps since Q has zero sections there. U and V cover X because x belongs to U. Apply TopCat.Sheaf.existsUnique_gluing with the Bool-indexed cover to obtain a global section q with the prescribed restriction.

For any lift s of q, naturality shows that its restriction to U minus sU lies in the kernel of the quotient map on U. The inclusion i is mono because its composite with I.toModulesι is J.toModulesι, so i and its cokernel form a short exact sequence. Evaluation at U preserves finite limits and is additive, hence is exact at the middle. Obtain a section of J(U) mapping to the difference. Its residue at x is zero since x belongs to Z prime. As sU maps to 1, the residue of s on U is 1. The germ restriction identity transports the same equality to the global section.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_closedPoint_ideal_quotient_section (X : Scheme.{u})
    (U : X.Opens) (x : X) (hxU : x ∈ U)
    (hx : IsClosed ({x} : Set X)) :
    let Z : TopologicalSpace.Closeds X := ⟨(U : Set X)ᶜ, U.isOpen.isClosed_compl⟩
    let Z' : TopologicalSpace.Closeds X := ⟨(U : Set X)ᶜ ∪ {x},
      U.isOpen.isClosed_compl.union hx⟩
    let I := Scheme.IdealSheafData.vanishingIdeal Z
    let J := Scheme.IdealSheafData.vanishingIdeal Z'
    let i : J.toModules ⟶ I.toModules := Scheme.IdealSheafData.toModulesOfLE
      (Scheme.IdealSheafData.vanishingIdeal_antimono
        (show Z ≤ Z' from Set.subset_union_left))
    ∃ (q : Γ(cokernel i, ⊤)), ∀ (s : Γ(I.toModules, ⊤)),
      (cokernel.π i).app ⊤ s = q →
        X.evaluation ⊤ x (by trivial) (I.toModulesι.app ⊤ s) = 1
